A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlatQuant study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization accuracy, perplexity, inference latency, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Qwen evaluations, training-time flatness trajectories, and further latency comparisons.

M1.justification: The learned affine transformations, Kronecker decomposition, channel scaling, clipping, blockwise reconstruction objective, and fused kernel remain unchanged. The new flatness metric measures training behavior; it does not replace or augment the training loss.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText-2, C4, the six commonsense benchmarks, MT-Bench, and Pile in the calibration analysis. The added Qwen evaluations reuse existing benchmarks and introduce model configurations without new data or task requirements.

E2.justification: Figures 4 and 6 and the appendix speedup plots add FlatQuant without kernel fusion as a comparator. This variant previously appeared in kernel profiling, but was absent from these corresponding comparisons. Existing external baseline memberships are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen-2.5-Instruct 7B/32B configurations, measures flatness during training in four selected LLaMA-3-8B blocks, and adds unfused controls to latency experiments. The original calibration recipe and benchmark evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 and Figure 8 add trajectories relating flatness to reconstruction error. Fusion analysis extends from kernel profiling to additional end-to-end controls, while Figures 16–17 add query, key, value, and down-projection distribution examples. These supplement the retained component, calibration, clipping, and low-bit analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Random sampling and averaging over inputs remain unchanged; the new training curves do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 11 newly reports Qwen results: for 32B, FlatQuant RTN averages 74.89% QA accuracy versus 75.10% for FP16 and 72.25% for QuaRot-GPTQ. New unfused results include 2.11x prefill speedup at batch size 64, alongside the retained 2.30x fused result. Flatness trajectories and additional distribution results are also added; existing numerical tables are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 introduces a mathematical flatness definition using MSE from an equal-magnitude vector with the same L2 norm. Appendix C.5 adds a parameter-count and memory derivation. Existing method equations and derivations remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about flatness, learnable transformations, near-lossless LLaMA-3-70B quantization, and inference speedups. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix C.1 interprets the joint reduction in flatness error and reconstruction loss as evidence explaining optimization. Section 4.3 now attributes QuaRot-comparable speed without fusion to Kronecker decomposition. Appendix E retains the same calibration-selection and unexplored-data-type limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix C.5 newly documents per-transformation parameter counts and a per-block memory calculation yielding about 0.11MB for LLaMA-2-7B. Existing optimizer settings, calibration details, SVD/AMP implementation, kernel instructions, and code access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the SkVQ citation by Duanmu et al. and a brief related-work statement acknowledging searched or learned clipping thresholds. Its broader positioning against scaling, rotation, and AffineQuant remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the name's dual meaning, makes localized prose revisions, and inserts the flatness subsection before the existing appendix experiments. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 11 and Figures 8, 16, and 17; expands latency plots with unfused series and corresponding legends; and adjusts some plotting ticks and spacing. Existing displays are otherwise retained, with appendix renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The quantitative flatness trajectories strengthen the existing mechanism argument, the unfused controls clarify the sources of speedup, and Qwen results extend validation beyond LLaMA. These provide a modest overall improvement to an already detailed study. A limited weakness is that the new 0.11MB memory estimate derives from a per-block calculation, while Section 3.1 leaves that scope unclear.
